goal: Migrate Ledger Account Categories to the managed Effect runtime without changing HTTP, domain, error, persistence, transaction, concurrency, identifier, timestamp, tenancy, or operational behavior.

tasks.name: Verify the Organization-scoping prerequisite
tasks.description: Block implementation until the separate Organization-scoping design and plan exist and are approved. Confirm that the Effect migration lands first against the recorded Ledger-only baseline and that Organization-scoping code follows in its own change set. If the approved ordering or Category method signatures differ, stop and rebaseline this migration before changing production code.

tests: Both named Organization-scoping artifacts exist and form an approved, decision-complete plan.
The approved ordering keeps Organization-scoping implementation outside this migration change set.
acceptance: T2 cannot start while either prerequisite artifact is missing or unapproved.
The Category baseline and internal signatures remain valid for a migration-first ordering.
No Organization-scoping code is added by this plan.

tasks.name: Characterize uncovered legacy behavior
inputs: Current Promise repository, service, routes, and PostgreSQL test fixtures
Current test inventory of 38 repository, 13 service, and 39 route cases
tasks.description: Add test-only characterization before changing production code. Lock the behaviors most exposed by the adapter and execution-model change: malformed stored metadata, PostgreSQL-owned creation time, application-owned update time, preservation of created time on upsert, read-before-upsert order, last-writer-wins replacement, delete-between-read-and-upsert recreation, relationship failure precedence, unexpected row-decoding failure, and database unavailability remaining a generic internal server response. Preserve the existing test inventory and assertions.

acceptance: All new characterization tests pass against the legacy Promise implementation.
No production file changes in T2.
Existing JWT 401, readonly-token 403, CRUD, relationship, and error assertions remain present.

tasks.name: Cut the complete Category slice over to Effect
inputs: Green legacy characterization suite from T2
Existing Category entity and TypeBox-derived request type
tasks.description: Perform one compile-green production cutover because splitting repository, service, plugin, runtime, and route removal creates known invalid intermediate states. Replace the Promise repository with an Effect contract, tag, live implementation, and Layer backed by DatabaseTag.effectDb. Convert all eight repository operations while preserving exact SQL and sequential statement order. Convert all nine service operations and preserve the separate update existence read followed by ID-based upsert. Compose the service into the existing runtime, remove only Category from legacy repository and service plugins and fixtures, and run every route through server.runtime. Adapt the focused tests without removing baseline assertions. Repository and service Effects use unknown failures: expected shared NotFoundError and ConflictError values, native adapter failures, and synchronous TypeID, entity, or response-conversion throws enter the failure channel unchanged and never become defects or ServiceUnavailableError values.

tests: Repository tests run through the Category Layer and preserve CRUD, Ledger isolation, upsert, cascade, relationship, sequencing, timestamp, metadata, and failure cases.
Service tests use an Effect repository Layer and preserve delegation, entity construction, update ordering, races, and original failure objects.
Route success and service-failure cases use an isolated Fastify server with Layer.succeed.
Existing invalid-JWT 401 and readonly-token 403 cases continue through buildServer and its real authentication and permission hooks.
A failing native adapter and a synchronous conversion throw are failures rather than defects and reach the existing handler as generic 500 responses.
acceptance: The package typechecks at the end of the cutover; no completed task leaves broken consumers or temporary compatibility code.
All nine routes preserve their methods, paths, permissions, schemas, operation IDs, statuses, headers, response bodies, and error details.
Create remains 200 without Location; every other mutation remains 200 with its existing body.
List remains Ledger-scoped, created-descending, and offset/limit paginated.
Update remains a nontransactional existence read followed by ID-based upsert with last-writer-wins and delete/recreate behavior.
Link Account reads the Category then inserts without pre-reading the Account; unlink Account reads the Category then deletes.
Link parent reads child then parent, checks direct equality, then inserts; unlink parent reads only the child then deletes.
No Organization predicate, transaction, concurrency combinator, lock, retry, idempotency key, schema change, new runtime, generic executor, or reusable test harness is introduced.
Settlement, Statement, and Balance Monitor legacy wiring remains unchanged.

tasks.name: Run CI and audit behavior deviations
tasks.description: Run the full repository CI once after the focused suites have passed. Compare the final diff with the recorded baseline and stop if it contains any unplanned HTTP, domain, error, SQL, transaction, concurrency, identifier, timestamp, tenancy, or operational change.

acceptance: The final diff contains only the files owned by T2 and T3.
Entity code, TypeBox schemas, database schema, migrations, dependencies, and unrelated slices are unchanged.
The final route, service, and repository assertion inventory is at least the characterized baseline.
Organization scoping, OCC, lock_version, transactions, retries, idempotency keys, real balances, cycle detection, and relationship hardening remain outside this change set.
Any discovered deviation returns to design or planning before implementation continues.
